usagePolicy.rule: Consumers choose a registered component and pass documented props only. They must not add local CSS for a component or pass raw colors, spacing, radius, shadow, icon paths, or state styling.
usagePolicy.exceptions: Only component-specific geometry explicitly registered in COMPONENTS.md and the executable contract may differ from the Foundation scale.

implementation.notes: Use the existing Panda wrapper. Do not recreate button anatomy or translate Catalog variants directly without checking Panda props.
Panda Chip does not cover the Catalog 24px geometry or semantic button behavior. Use the React design-system adapter; never use Chip as a checkbox or radio replacement.
Panda Tag does not guarantee the Catalog close affordance, size scale, or semantic tones. Use the React design-system adapter for compact descriptive labels.
Use Panda Checkbox for semantic multi-select choices and its documented group API.
Use Panda Checkbox.Group for controlled groups; product-specific option data and validation remain outside the primitive.
Use Panda Radio or Radio.Group for one-of-many choices rather than custom selected rows.

Panda Selection does not cover the Catalog content types, selected marker, or radio and checkbox semantics. Use the React design-system adapter; use standalone Radio or Checkbox when a compact control is sufficient.

Use the React design-system adapter for Catalog size, shape, field status, controlled or uncontrolled opening, single or range selection, month navigation, and disabled days with YYYY-MM-DD values. Booking availability and timezone policy remain product concerns.
Use the React design-system adapter for placement, arrowless mode, focus behavior, and delayed hover presentation; do not make a Tooltip the only access path to essential content.
Use the Panda wrapper and an existing reviewed modal flow. Confirm focus restoration and custom footer behavior before extending it.
Use the React design-system adapter for Catalog-owned trigger modes, placement, outside dismissal, Escape behavior, and leave delay. Do not use Popup as an unreviewed menu or modal substitute.
Use the React design-system adapter for a local consequential action, controlled or uncontrolled open state, outside dismissal, Escape behavior, loading, and confirmation callbacks.
Use the existing Panda wrapper for structural separation and labelled dividers.

Use the React design-system adapter for the Catalog size scale, image fallback, flag placement, logo treatment, and avatar-group overlap. Panda remains an internal implementation option, not the product import boundary.
Use the React design-system adapter for Catalog count, dot, status, overflow, and anchor behavior. Panda remains an internal implementation option, not the product import boundary.
Use the React design-system adapter for collapsed overflow, current-page semantics, and Catalog separator behavior. Page routing remains product-owned.
Use the React design-system adapter for the Catalog surface, media-ratio, density, and interactive-card contract. Business objects such as teacher cards remain composed product patterns.
Use the Panda wrapper for persistent in-context feedback, not field validation or transient notification behavior.
Use the React design-system adapter for Catalog labels, count treatment, trailing action, and automatic or manual keyboard activation.

Use the React design-system adapter for supplied page lists, ellipsis treatment, controlled current page, and disabled boundary actions. Page fetches, route state, and total-result semantics stay product-owned.
Use the React design-system adapter for Catalog half-step, clearable, preview, label, and keyboard rating behavior. Do not calculate rating aggregates in the component.

Use the React design-system Sidebar for controlled or local collapse, Pin and More movement, same-list drag ordering, bounded More disclosure, section animation, and internal smooth scrolling. Product adapters still supply destinations, state, approved icons, persistence, route behavior, and analytics.
Use the React design-system adapter for supplied values, affixes, descriptions, and loading presentation. Formatting and calculation remain product-owned.
Use the React design-system adapter for supplied columns, row headers, compact density, loading, empty state, and responsive overflow. Sorting, pagination, and selection remain product-owned.
Use the React design-system adapter for supplied event history, semantic dot tones, pending state, labels, reverse order, and alternate layout. Event meaning remains caller-owned.

Use the React design-system TopNav, TopNavContext, and TopNavSearch for its three-slot 72px shell, centred search expansion, language/context menu, and reviewed icon geometry. Product adapters still supply navigation meaning, query effects, language state, account actions, routes, and analytics.
Use the React design-system adapter for single, range, vertical, reverse, disabled, tooltip, and controlled slider presentation. Domain values and validation remain product behavior.
Use the React design-system adapter for a titled content surface, supplied extra action, density, and optional structural divider. Avoid decorative nested cards.
Use Panda Input.Search for the field surface. Query timing, suggestions, results, and route synchronization require product behavior.
Use the Panda wrapper for confirmed selection behavior; option data, remote search, and business filters remain product-owned.
Use the React design-system adapter for immediate binary changes, semantic switch behavior, and the Catalog 44px control geometry. Persistence and confirmation remain caller-owned.
Use the Panda wrapper with an existing reviewed drawer flow; route, focus, dismissal, and responsive content behavior must be verified.
Use Panda Form.Item for labels, help text, validation display, and required state around supported controls.
Use the Panda wrapper for text entry. Prefix, suffix, validation, and controlled value behavior must follow the current API.
Use Panda Input.TextArea for multiline entry and rely on its verified count, read-only, and status behavior.
Use the React design-system adapter for Catalog size, shape, bounds, increment controls, and controlled numeric entry. Unit semantics and validation messages remain product behavior.
Use the React design-system adapter for searchable single selection, query, loading, option groups, size, shape, and status. Fetching, ranking, and query policy remain product behavior.

implementation.notes: Use the React design-system adapter for dropzone, trigger, avatar upload, local file list presentation, remove actions, complete/uploading/error states, and client-side selection. Upload targets, validation policy, server progress, and file lifecycle remain product-owned.
Use the React design-system adapter for default and flow-progress step anatomy, orientation, current state, disabled steps, and controlled navigation. Completion rules remain in the flow adapter.
Use the React design-system adapter for supplied progress values, default/success/error status, indeterminate loading, and accessible progress semantics. Completion meaning remains product-owned.
Use Panda message for transient feedback. Application context, queueing, duration, and recovery actions must follow a reviewed product pattern.
Use the Panda notification API for persistent transient feedback and keep product outcomes and actions in the caller.
Use Panda Result for terminal or recoverable outcome presentation; the next action remains a product decision.
Use the React design-system adapter for Catalog text, content, avatar, button, input, image, and card placeholders. It honors reduced motion; do not use it to hide missing required content.

Use the React design-system adapter for menu placement, open state, icon sizing, disabled and destructive items, and keyboard dismissal. Item meaning, permissions, and analytics remain product behavior.
Use the React design-system adapter for accordion/details anatomy, open state, disabled behavior, and the approved 24px disclosure icon.
Use the React design-system adapter for the Catalog 32/40/48 geometry, rounded or pill shape, and immediate selected-mode state.

Use the React design-system primitive for availability and option appearances, booking locks, duration, selected state, loading, and delayed tooltips. Booking permissions and availability data remain product behavior.

Use the React design-system adapter for controlled or uncontrolled open state, option-grid sizing, TimeSlot presentation, selected values, disabled state, and Escape/outside dismissal. Availability, timezone, and bookable-duration rules remain product-owned.

Use the React design-system adapter for availability, teacher availability, compact availability, and lesson record views. It owns responsive day columns, sticky date headers, scrollable time areas, TimeSlot state, one-hour selection from 15-minute cells, week/date switching, and tooltip placement. Availability data, booking policy, timezone conversion, and lesson history retrieval remain product behavior.
Use the React design-system Footer for its reviewed layout and accessible link groups. Footer links, locale, legal copy, social destinations, and utility controls remain product-supplied content.
Use the React design-system adapter for reviewed contextual floating content. It shares Popup placement, trigger, dismissal, and hover-delay behavior; keep trigger meaning and actions in the caller.
